newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Transrapid to hold news conference 1700 GMT.
newsitem.headline: German Transrapid to hold news conference 1700 GMT.

text.p: Companies involved in Germany's planned Transrapid high-speed train will hold a press conference at 1700 GMT to comment on the project, a spokesman for consortium leader Thyssen AG said on Wednesday.
The spokesman for the engineering group said that Eckhard Rohkamm, the head of Thyssen Industrie AG, would be commenting on the Transrapid magnetic levitation rail project at the press conference.

The spokesman went on to say that the meeting being held at Frankfurt Airport was "purely routine" and would not reveal whether details about the future of the project would be released at the press conference.
Earlier on Wednesday the German newspaper Handelsblatt reported that the future of the project was in jeopardy.
Handelsblatt said new projections showed that Transrapid would have to charge much higher fares than previously believed, making it uneconomic. The newspaper did not cite the source of its new data.
A government study analysing the costs and viability of the rail project, planned to run between Berlin and Hamburg, is due for release at the end of March.
The total cost of the project is officially estimated at nine billion marks but critics charge it will inevitably cost a lot more.
